1329 Fiest Fifth Street
Los Angeles, California
August 5, 1940
Sen. Sherican Downey
united States senator
Mashington, D. G.
My dear Senator:
I feel confident that you, as one pledged by oath to support the
Constitution, will want to investigate the charges made by Federal authori-
ties against the religious organization, the "I AM" Activity, of using
the mails to defraud.
To my knowledge and that of all with whom I have
talked, who have been in the organization since its very inception, the
leaders of this thoroughly patriotic and educational (rather than religious)
movement, have never asked for a nickel from any of their followers, which
is quite contrary to the practices of most organizations of any kind whatso-
ever!

LoA. 36-138
The indictment alleges that GUY W. BALLARD, who died at
Ios Angeles, California, on Deçember 29, 1939, was représented by
the defendants to have been selected by the alleged "ascended master"
Saint Germain, as a divine messenger, and it was represented that the
words of the alleged divine entity, saint Germain, would be trans-
citted to mankind through the relium of the said GUY W. BALLARD. The
indictment alleges that EDNA W. ALLARD (wife of GUY VI. BALLARD) and
DONALD BALLARD( Son of GUY W. BiLLAKD) were stated to have been
selected as divine messengers through whom the words of the alleged
"ascerded masters"
including the alleged Saint Germain, would be
communicated to mankind under the teachings commonly known as the
"I AN" movement, It is stated that the defendants represented that
the various books which were written by GUY W. BALLARD were dictated
by Saint Germain and sold urder such representations. It is stated
that GUY F. BALLARD, during his lifetime, and EDNA T. BALLARD and
DONALD BALLARD had claimed to have attained e supernatural state of
self-inmortality, which condition enabled them, and each of them, to
be entirely free from ailments common to man, and to conquer disease,
death, old age, poverty, and misery, which power or condition and
supernatural state the defendants and each of them, represented they
could and would transmit to others willing to pay therefor or willing
to part with other things of value therefor to the defendants. It is
alleged that all these representations were made for the false and
fraudulent purpose of securing money or other things of value from the
persons intended to be defrauded, and that the defendants knew the
representations to be false.
The principal office of the two corporations mai ained by
the BALLARDS is in Chii*
These corporations are know a SAINT
GERLAIN FOUNDATION" an OJAINT GERVAIN PRESS",
However, th. krincipal
revenues of the corpor "Juns were obtained in the Los Angeles vicinity
and a branch office was maintained in Los Angeles. The greater part
of three separate sets of books have already come into the possession
of the Post Office Inspectors, those of the SAINT GERMAIN FOUNDATION,
Chicago, and both the Chicago and Los Angeles records of the SAINT
GERMAIN PRESS.
The persons other than the BALLARDS named in the indict-
ment are their associates who aided them in preaching the doctrines of
the "I AM" movement and in collecting funds from members of the move-
ment.

{"alpha_words": 312, "chars": 1969, "method": "ocr", "page": 129, "variant": "plain-vision"}
LIte 36-138
The purpose of the accounting investigation, in this case
is to determine the anount and source of cash receipts and the amount
and reasons for cash disbursements broken down in so far as possible
to skow the benefit to the various defendants.
The investigation to date indicates that cash receipts
and disbursements are handled by both the SAINT GERMAIN FOUNDATION
and the SAINT GERMAIN PRESS and that there are a large number of
intercompany transections.
It also appears that prior to the in-
corporation of the SAINI GERMAIN PRESS on December 19, 1939, consider.
able of the business of the "I AM" movement was shown in the personal
records of the BALLARDS which have not and probably will not be pro-
duced for examination. In order that a proper classification of cash
disbursements may be made it appears that it will be necessary, to
examine thousands of receipts and memoranda, some of which have not
already been produced. A request for the missing records has been
made on the defendants! attorneys by the United States Attorney and
it is stated that the missing corporate records will be produced in
Los Angeles.
In addition tọ the examination ot the records of the SAINI
GERMAIN FOUNDATIN and the SAINT GERMAIN PRESS, it appears that it may
be desirable to exemine the records of the TEDDAHL ADVERTISING AGENCY,
Los Angeles, whioh árranged the radio broadcasts for the "I AM" move-
ment and also the records of R. R. DONNELLEY & SONS COMPANY, Chicago,
Illinois, which published the books of the "I AM" movement.
The trial of this case has been set for lovember 19, 1940,
and it is estimated that the greater part of the intervoning time will
be réquired to complete the examination as above outlined.
Special Agent JAMES C, SLOANE and the writer performed in-
vestigatite activity in connection with the case.
Special Agent SLOANE
worked from September 4, to 14; 1940, while the writer worked on
September 4; 6, 9, 10 and 14, 1940•

in maxing plant surveys on two plants within this district.

1940, on which date he will leave for Chicago, Illinois.

proceeded to trial against EDNA VI. BALLARD, DONALD BALLARD, BETTY MUNDY,
FRANK VON DERHOYA, CHARLES SINDELAR, PEARL SINDELAR, VILLIAN J. CASSIERE,
PAUL STICKELL and GRANT Ii. LEWIS.
At the close of the Government!s case on January 3, 1941,
Federal Judge ISON YANKICH dismissed the indictment against GRANT İ.
ISIS. The presenting of evidence was concluded and the Judge charged
the jury on January 16, 1941. The jury remained locked up from that
date until Januäry 20, 1941 when the Judge dismissed them after they
had stated they were in hopeless disagreement.
At that time the jury
advised that they had reached the verdict of "not guilty! for CHARLES
SINDELAR, PEARL SINDELAR and FRANK VON DERHOYA, and that they were in
disagreement as to EDMA W. BALLARD, DONALD BALLARD, BETTY MUNDY, PAUL
STICKELL, GRANT L. LEVIS and WILLIAM J. CASSIERE.
The Judge then dis-
missed the jury.

Agent JAMES A. SLOAN prépared a number of revised schedules to be in-

cided not to call the accountant, B. A. JACKSON, as a Government witness:

jects, as well as the sale of books upon the part. of Defendants STICKELL
and CASSIERE:

General,

been engaged in subversive activities at the instigation of the
Cormunist Party, and that rumors had begun that the cult is to

instructions of the Conmunist Party; and, that a confidential
informant at Santa fe, New Mexico, had advised that the cult
has been requested to block all highways and railroads with •
their private cars to prevent troop and material movements. It
vas also related that Mrs. DICK ABDIE, 49 Scoett Street, San.
Francisco, California, had received a letter from the headquarters
of this cult, place not known; informing that the entire Pacific
Coast tould be bombed on February 12, 1942, which is a Japanese
holiday.

certain members of this cult be interviewed openly concerning!
the above-mentioned rumors.

Mrs: BALLARD advised that the decrees of the "I AM" Cult

stated that this organization is very patriotic, and in all of
their meetings Americanism is taught. She advised that the rumor

foundation in fact. She stated that the cult has so few friends

was any information of interest developed he Hould immediately con-

Mail Fraud.
Dear Sir:
Attached hereto are copies of papers received from censors
indicating that members of the "I Al" are causing their publications
and literature to be mailed by parcel post from Mexico to addressees
within the jurisdiction of the United States. An existing fruad
order prohibits the entry of this matter in the United States mails.
This matter vas discussed with the local post office in-
spectors by Special Agent THOWAS I. MULHERIN and they stated that
the Mexican mailing constitutes a violation of the fraud order. It
was suggested that this matter be forwarded to the Postmaster General,
for the attention of Post Office Inspector W. F. CALLAHAN, who is
handling the matter for the Post Office Department.
In view of the request for transmission to the Postmaster
General the papers in question are being forarded to you.
Very truly yours,
RB.
